chorley: Beyond the town-centre rooms, Chorley's calendar leans on its parks and grassroots circuit. ChorFest fills the grounds of Astley Park with tribute and local acts, while Chorley Live spreads more than 200 artists across upwards of 35 pubs and small venues over a single weekend, and Astley Hall hosts its own programme of cultural events. The wider catchment pulls in crews from Leyland, Adlington and Euxton, with the West Pennine Moors as a backdrop. Every park stage and town-centre room keeps local production and front-of-house crews busy.
farnham: Farnham's events life runs through Farnham Maltings on Bridge Square, one of the busiest arts centres in Surrey, where the 410-seat Great Hall handles music, comedy and festivals and the Cellar Bar and Tindle Studio take the more intimate bills. The town sits in a strong catchment alongside Aldershot, Godalming and Guildford, drawing on the wider Surrey Hills and the Bourne for outdoor and community events. From the larger hall to the studio rooms, the programme keeps independent production and front-of-house crews busy across the year.
coatbridge: Coatbridge centres much of its public events life on Summerlee, the Museum of Scottish Industrial Life, a twenty-acre site whose grounds host the long-running Summerlee Model Railway Show, family weekends and seasonal gatherings beside the restored ironworks and tramway. The town sits within easy reach of Airdrie, Bellshill and the wider Monklands, feeding a Lanarkshire catchment of community festivals and outdoor events. From museum-ground programmes to hall bookings across the borough, the calendar keeps local production and front-of-house crews busy through the season.
margate: Margate's live-events engine is Dreamland, whose four spaces span the indoor Hall by the Sea, Ballroom and Roller Room and the open-air Scenic Stage Arena built for the biggest outdoor concerts and festival bills. The wider Thanet catchment pulls in crews from Ramsgate, Broadstairs and Cliftonville, with grassroots rooms and street events across the old town adding to the load. From the arena's festival-scale productions to the indoor halls, the programme keeps production and front-of-house crews busy right through the warmer months.
sutton-in-ashfield: Sutton-in-Ashfield's events scene has grown around the Cornerstone Theatre and Portland Square in the regenerated town centre, with Kings Mill Reservoir and the Mill Adventure Base hosting outdoor and waterside activity. The wider Ashfield and Mansfield catchment carries much of the bigger programming, from the One Call Stadium country music bills to the Palace Theatre, drawing crews from Kirkby-in-Ashfield, Mansfield and Hucknall. From town-centre stages to reservoir-side events, the calendar keeps local production and front-of-house crews busy across the season.
feltham: Feltham's events life leans on its green spaces and community calendar, with Bedfont Lakes Country Park and its lakes, woodland and meadows hosting outdoor activity, and Bedfont Sports Club taking event bookings. The Feltham, Hanworth and Bedfont Festival and the West London Turkish Festival bring food, live music and dance to the area, while Feltham Arts runs a community programme. Sitting within Hounslow alongside Hanworth, Bedfont and Ashford, the calendar keeps local production and front-of-house crews busy through the warmer months.
llanelli: Llanelli's events spread well beyond the Ffwrnes on Park Street. The Selwyn Samuel Centre near Park Crescent turns over to concerts, exhibitions and craft markets through the summer recess, while Parc Howard's parkland hosts annual family fun days north of the centre, and the 15,000-seat Parc y Scarlets at Pemberton handles stadium-scale events. The wider Carmarthenshire catchment ties in with Carmarthen's Lyric and Ammanford's Miners' under Theatrau Sir Gar. Across these venues and parks, local production and front-of-house crews stay busy.
ayr: Ayr's events reach well past the Gaiety on Carrick Street. The Burns Festival fills Rozelle Park in the grounds of Rozelle House, Ayr Racecourse stages the Scottish Grand National and Gold Cup festivals with their large crews, and Belleisle Gardens and Alloway's Burns heritage sites add to the calendar. The wider South Ayrshire catchment draws in Prestwick, Troon and the coast. From racecourse festival builds to park stages and theatre bills, local production and front-of-house crews stay busy through the season.
cwmbran: Cwmbran's events life runs through the Congress Theatre in the town centre and out to the Boating Lake, where a popular June community day brings a raft race, food and craft stalls and a full bill of music and dance, alongside the local Crow Fest. Neighbouring Pontypool adds its own big day in Pontypool Park, and the wider Torfaen catchment ties in Cwmbran, Pontypool and Blaenavon. Across theatre, lakeside and park events, local production and front-of-house crews stay busy through the season.
beckenham: Beckenham carries a real live-music heritage at Croydon Road Recreation Ground, whose restored Bowie Bandstand recalls the 1969 free festival and still hosts open-air concerts, while Beckenham Place Park has grown its own outdoor music programme. Just up the hill, Crystal Palace Park stages large summer festival bills, and the wider catchment ties in Bromley, Penge and Sydenham. From bandstand events to country-park festival stages, the calendar keeps local production and front-of-house crews busy right through the warmer months.
kirkcaldy: Kirkcaldy's events centre on the Adam Smith Theatre on Bennochy Road, the 475-seat heart of the local arts scene since 1899, refurbished in 2023 with the Beveridge Suite, the Exchange and the Spinning Top Cafe and Bar adding event spaces, and a Langtoun Jazz strand among its music bills. Beveridge Park gives the town its big open-air ground, and the wider Fife catchment draws in Glenrothes, Burntisland and Leven. Across theatre and park events, local production and front-of-house crews stay busy through the year.
lytham st annes: Lytham Festival is the headline, filling Lytham Green beside the windmill, a strip between the coastal road and the Ribble estuary, with several nights of major bills and a traditional promenade-style classical finale run by Cuffe and Taylor. Beyond it, the Lowther Pavilion and its gardens carry a year-round programme of shows on the Fylde Coast, and Lytham Hall hosts events in its grounds. The wider catchment ties in St Annes, Blackpool and Kirkham. Across green, pavilion and hall, production and front-of-house crews stay busy.
